issues.description: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame embeds a live FrameProcessor reference instead of a stable identifier
issues.detail: The `service` field holds a mutable FrameProcessor instance on a value-like control frame. This complects value with runtime identity, breaks serialization/logging, creates lifecycle/GC coupling, and invites equality surprises. Carry a stable service id or name string and resolve at the switcher edge.

issues.description: Targeting check `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` relies on default object identity equality
issues.detail: FrameProcessor falls back to identity-based __eq__. If a subclass overrides equality, or the active service is wrapped/replaced, the suppression silently fails open and the control frame leaks downstream. Use `is`, or compare by a stable id, and document the invariant explicitly.

issues.description: Forward-reference annotation `"FrameProcessor"` is unresolved and unimported in frames.py
issues.detail: The string annotation works at dataclass construction time but any `get_type_hints`, pydantic adapter, or IDE introspection will fail to resolve it. It also signals an entangled module boundary that a string service id would make honest. Add a TYPE_CHECKING import or switch the field to a value type.

issues.description: STTService now re-pushes the request frame instead of consuming it, splitting the protocol
issues.detail: STTService and its mock call `_push_stt_metadata()` then `push_frame(frame)`, relying on the switcher to swallow on target match. Outside a switcher the frame escapes downstream, and the handle-then-re-push contract is undocumented. Either consume at the service or route only at the switcher — not both.

issues.description: Public rename ships without a backward-compatible deprecation alias
issues.detail: `RequestMetadataFrame` was an exported symbol; renaming it outright breaks downstream imports on the next version. A one-line alias plus a DeprecationWarning costs nothing and avoids triaging import errors for users. The changelog entry alone is insufficient for a public API break.

issues.description: Non-active-target path and suppression invariant are implicit, with no test or comment
issues.detail: The new branch returns only on match; the mismatch path passes through downstream by inference. The implicit invariant — "the request frame only arrives here after being handled by the active service" — needs a literate one-line comment and at least one explicit test, otherwise a future broadcast refactor will cause duplicate emission.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously identifies the same core taste flaw: a control frame should carry a stable identifier, not a live FrameProcessor handle. This complecting of value with runtime identity, combined with default-equality-based targeting in the switcher, is the principal NEEDS-WORK item. Secondary concerns also align across reviewers — an unresolved forward-reference annotation, a split handle-then-re-push protocol between STTService and the switcher, missing back-compat alias for the public rename, and an under-documented suppression invariant. The rename direction and test coverage are sound; the implementation reached for the easy answer rather than the simple one.
